references.text: Nehemiah describes how the people brought branches from olive trees, wild olive trees, myrtle trees, palm trees, and other leafy trees to build booths, fulfilling the command in Leviticus 23:40.
The context is the Feast of Tabernacles, which lasts seven days, where verse 40 is part of the instructions for the celebration.
Deuteronomy repeats the command to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days and rejoice before the Lord.
It explains the purpose of the Feast of Tabernacles—to remind Israel that they lived in booths when God brought them out of Egypt.
The command to rejoice before the Lord your God, which corresponds to 'usemachtem lifnei YHWH' (and you shall rejoice before the Lord).
John's Gospel mentions that the Feast of Tabernacles (ἡ σκηνοπηγία) was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem to celebrate it.
On the last great day of the Feast of Tabernacles, Jesus called out for living water, connecting to the water ceremony during the feast.
The crowd standing before the throne with palm branches (φοίνικες) in their hands, which may allude to the palm fronds used during the Feast of Tabernacles.
The psalmist mentions binding the festival offering with cords to the horns of the altar, traditionally linked to the Feast of Tabernacles and processions with branches.
